step-by-step-guide.title: Step-by-step Guide on how to grow Wolffia globosa

sections.title: Understanding Wolffia globosa
sections.text: Wolffia globosa, also known as Asian watermeal or duckweed, is the world's smallest flowering plant. It floats on the water surface and grows rapidly under the right conditions. This plant is valued for its high protein content and its ability to help purify water. Successful cultivation requires careful control of environment, nutrients, and water quality.

sections.title: Choosing the Right Growing Environment
sections.text: Wolffia globosa thrives in warm, nutrient-rich, stagnant or slow-moving freshwater. For home or farm cultivation, use a controlled body of water (aquarium, pond, trough) that’s clean and free of contaminants.

pesticide-contamination.title: Pesticide Contamination
pesticide-contamination.tagline: If your pond is near a rice field or plantation, always check water sources — clean water = safe duckweed = safe consumers.

sections.text: Pesticide contamination happens when chemicals used on nearby farms wash into your pond via rain runoff or contaminated sources.

sections.title: Common Sources
items: Runoff from nearby plantations or rice fields
Water pumped from canals collecting farm runoff

sections.title: How to Prevent
items: Avoid water from areas near sprayed fields
Prefer safe sources: 1) properly stored rainwater 2) clean well/groundwater 3) tested/filtered canal or pond water
Be extra cautious after heavy rain
Do not reuse water from other farms unless chemical-free

sections.title: Risks to Your Duckweed & Consumers
items: Residues can make duckweed unsafe to eat
Long-term pond contamination may require full replacement

heavy-metal-contamination.title: Heavy Metal Contamination
heavy-metal-contamination.tagline: Just because water looks clean doesn’t mean it’s safe. Choose water sources wisely to protect your duckweed and your customers.

sections.title: What is Heavy Metal Contamination?
sections.text: Heavy metals like lead, cadmium, mercury, and arsenic can enter your pond if water comes from industrial areas, old mining zones, or polluted canals/rivers. They’re invisible and odorless—testing is required.

sections.title: Common Sources
items: Canals/rivers near factories or industrial estates
Runoff from old mining or waste sites
Irrigation water flowing through many farm zones

sections.title: How to Prevent
items: Avoid unknown/untested sources, especially near industrial zones
Prefer: 1) clean well/groundwater 2) properly stored rainwater 3) sources verified by advisors/authorities
Get water tested if unsure or in historically polluted areas

sections.title: Risks to Your Duckweed & Consumers
items: Duckweed becomes unsafe to eat (metal buildup)
Contamination can persist even after water changes
Potential harm to animals or people consuming it

overuse-of-NPK.title: Overuse of Chemical Fertilizers (NPK)
overuse-of-NPK.tagline: Fertilizer is food, not a cure. Too much can do more harm than good. Watch your duckweed, check your data, and apply only what’s needed.

sections.title: What is Overuse of Chemical Fertilizers (NPK)?
sections.text: NPK helps when used correctly. Overuse can destabilize your pond—leading to unhealthy duckweed and poor water quality.

sections.title: How to Apply NPK Safely
items: Follow recommended dosage for pond size/density

sections.title: Risks to Your Duckweed & Pond
items: Excess nutrients suffocate duckweed and boost harmful algae
Possible need for full pond cleaning

user-of-organic-fertilizers.title: Use of Organic Fertilizers (Animal Waste)
user-of-organic-fertilizers.tagline: Just because it’s organic doesn’t mean it’s safe. Avoid animal waste in ponds to protect your duckweed and your health.

sections.title: What is Organic Fertilizers (Animal Waste)?
sections.text: Using animal manure (pig, cow, chicken) can introduce dangerous bacteria and pathogens, making duckweed unsafe.

sections.title: Common Issues from Animal Waste Use
Safer Organic Alternatives
items: Choose plant-based compost or treated bio-fertilizers
Never apply raw animal waste directly
Maintain pond hygiene and clean water flow

sections.title: Risks to Your Duckweed & Consumers
items: May require full draining and cleaning
